title: Kenya VAT Rate Changes Timeline 2013-2026
description: Every change to Kenya's VAT rates since the VAT Act 2013 commenced: standard rate movements, the petroleum rate, and the 2026 taxation of payment processing services.
attribution: SmartVAT Kenya (smartvatkenya.co.ke), compiled from the VAT Act 2013 (Cap. 476), Finance Acts 2018-2026, and KRA public guidance.

records.detail: The VAT Act 2013 replaces the VAT Act (Cap. 481). Standard rate stays at 16%; zero-rated and exempt lists are restructured into the First and Second Schedules.
records.legalBasis: VAT Act 2013 (Cap. 476), s.5 and Third Schedule

records.detail: After public opposition to the Finance Act 2018's initial reinstatement of VAT on petroleum at 16%, Parliament reduced the rate on petroleum oils (kerosene, jet fuel and related products) from 16% to 8%.
records.correction: Rate shown as 8% for petroleum products; the general standard rate remained 16%.

records.detail: The Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2020 cuts the standard VAT rate from 16% to 14% as pandemic relief, alongside PAYE and turnover tax relief.
records.legalBasis: Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2020, Third Schedule amendment

records.detail: The 14% relief period ends; the standard rate returns to 16% with effect from 1 January 2021.
The 8% petroleum rate ends; petroleum oils are again taxed at the standard 16% rate.

records.change: Payment processing services move from exempt to 16%
records.detail: Payment processing, settlement, merchant acquiring, gateway and aggregation services supplied over a software platform become taxable at the standard rate. Fintechs must charge 16% VAT on these fees from this date.
